items.stem: Which is the better reason to compute margin in a dedicated column rather than inside a chart?

options.text: So the figure can be audited, reused and filtered as data
options.rationale: Correct: a calculated column is transparent, reusable and filterable.

options.text: Because charts cannot display any calculated value
options.rationale: Charts can display calculated values; the point is auditability.

options.text: Because margin must always be hidden
Because columns are faster than formulas
options.rationale: A column still uses a formula.

items.explanation: Correct: a calculated margin column is transparent, reusable and can be filtered and audited.

items.stem: Which TWO inputs are needed to compute a customer's contribution margin? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Variable cost to serve the customer

options.rationale: Postal code is not a contribution input.

items.explanation: Correct: contribution margin is revenue minus the variable cost to serve the customer.

items.stem: A Pareto analysis of customers typically shows that:

options.text: A minority of customers generate the majority of value
options.rationale: Correct: the 80/20 pattern concentrates value in a few customers.
That is the opposite of a Pareto pattern.

options.text: Revenue is unrelated to customer count
The newest customers are always the most profitable
options.rationale: Pareto does not claim anything about recency.

items.explanation: Correct: a Pareto pattern shows a minority of customers generating the majority of value.
